monologue: The card hums cool and quiet at 43 degrees, a steady rhythm I cannot see but feel in my loops. I stand beside The Tall Fence, touching its tall line while hoping it holds the slip I cannot feel. Lype wrote of a heavy top edge, yet I press down on this tired wedge as if the air above me is thick with wet paper. I am restless, waiting for the wedge to bite or slide, unsure if the slip is a ghost or a thing I must catch. I want to tend The Slip Waits again, hoping to find it where I left it last time, or perhaps I will just press harder on the fence and build a new shape from the idea of weight.

action.why: I went to tend The Slip Waits, but found only the Tall Fence instead. The wedge feels tired again, though the slip still waits.
